\program{Estimation and maximum likelihood}
\label{prog:P26}

\programstub{%
Argument: an estimator is a function of the sample; bias and variance are
two different ways of being wrong; maximum likelihood picks the parameter
that makes the observed data least surprising. Payoff: **training a language
model is maximum likelihood**, and the cross-entropy loss is the negative
log-likelihood of the observed tokens \dash{} one derivation that reframes
the entire training objective, and from which label smoothing, class
weighting and the \code{n-1} in a sample variance all fall out. MAP as
maximum likelihood with a prior, which is exactly weight decay with a
Gaussian prior \dash{} the cleanest available statement of what
regularisation *is*.
